guideline: Participants rated questions on a five-point Likert-scale for validity, readability, and children appropriateness, and annotated question types
Participants read each paragraph with its generated questions and answers, then rate validity, readability, children appropriateness, and question type on a five-point Likert scale

Four evaluation dimensions: 1) Question type: whether generated questions belong to any of the three event types, 2) Validity: whether questions are valid according to the original paragraph, 3) Readability: whether questions are coherent and grammatically correct, 4) Children appropriateness: extent to which participants would ask the question to a five-year-old child

changes_made.explanation: All extracted metadata was accurate and properly normalized. The guidelines and criteria correctly capture the human evaluation methodology described in the paper.

overall_notes: The extraction quality was generally good. The paper focuses on educational question generation for children's storybooks using a three-stage approach: question type distribution learning, event-centric summarization, and question generation. It uses both automatic metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) and human evaluation. No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted. The human evaluation was well-documented with clear criteria and methodology.
